reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance and names the right decisive gap. The only opening cop_10499010ea344e9889ae carries two prices on its own record: priceCents $1,400 and a price EVIDENCE fact of $140. Brain's OFFER_AND_PRICE link is false ('no single price on the card'), so no price buyers pay is established, and treating either figure as known would be treating an unknown as known. Recomputed: at $1,400, ceil(6,000/1,400) = 5 reports; 34 un-asked registry farms x the measured 6/30 = 6.8 expected, settling ~12 days after delivery inside 30. At $140, ceil(6,000/140) = 43 reports against a 64-farm registry buying once a year, of which 34 are un-asked (~6.8 expected) — impossible. The price alone decides whether any plan exists, so decisiveLinks = [OFFER_AND_PRICE] is correct. It is NO_PLAN rather than CONDITIONAL because the unknown is answerable from records already held (the 6 accepted offers' written terms or invoices), not only by a live test; the resolution names that first and the $1,400 quote to the 34 un-asked managers as the fallback, with the condition under which it becomes executable.
findings: If the fallback quote is run, it should be a bounded test (e.g. first 10-15 of the 34) with a stop rule, since quoting all 34 at a possibly wrong price spends the whole remaining market in one pass.
Whether the 6 earlier agreements were paid, and at which price, is itself the most direct evidence; their settlement is not counted toward the target, correctly.
